newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks seen shedding recent record gains.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks seen shedding recent record gains.

text.p: Dealers saw stocks opening with downside potential on Friday on momentum from profit-taking in late trade during Thursday's session.
"There are plenty of profits to take after gaining 7.5 percent the last three days, but we could soon rebound on strong foreign investor interest," one desk trader said.
Technical analysts placed support at 5,000 points on the IPC scale, down from Thursday's record close of 5,067.83.
Traders expected the peso to open near to prior closing levels with month-end demand for dollars easing as dealers awaited reaction to U.S. data and Thursday's dollar put auction by the central bank.
Dealers forecast a trading range of 7.8000/7.8300 per dollar for the 48-hour peso. Pre-open bids stood at 7.8150/7.8250 per dollar, compared to Thursday's close of 7.8130/7.8175.
Overnight rates on Cetes were seen opening down after speculation drove rates up to close at 21.00 percent on Thursday.
